title: This play may be completely sold out- but they do have a waitlist for...
transcript: What begins as just a normal day in first grade eventually turns into anything but as your teacher, Ms Joy, tells you that she is leaving for the remainder of the school year, and as the show goes on, has a bit of a mental breakdown as she slowly reveals to you the reasons why. That is the premise behind this viral, theatrical experience. The play is called Big Feelings and takes place in an apartment turned first grade classroom. When you arrive, you are assigned a character, can put your stuff in a cubby with your name on it, and are given a worksheet to fill out. And for about 90 minutes, you and 19 other audience members become students in Ms Joy's classroom. You take part in lessons ranging from math to reading to writing, each one revealing a little bit more about why Ms Joy is leaving. And I have to say, I think the overall presentation is incredibly effective here. Because it is such a small audience, you do build a bond with your group relatively quickly. And as your fellow students and Ms Joy herself become more familiar to you, this does start to feel like a class that you've taken before, and you start to revert back to a much simpler time. Yet at the same time as we're learning more about Ms Joy's backstory, some darker elements are slipping through, and the play takes on a darkly comedic tone as these darker Topics are being filtered through a first grade lens. I don't wanna say anything more out of risk of spoiling some of the twists and turns of the play, but overall this is the type of theatre that I crave. Theatre that can fully transport you to another time and place and let you just live in this new world, even just for a little bit. And while I do think this is definitely a case where the experience is better than the actual play itself, there is no denying that it is unlike any other play I've ever experienced. And for the sheer novelty of it, it is definitely a Broadway Ben recommendation.
